Hi Peter,
in your .RData, the object camOPTMatrix has all column names = NA. This is the reason for the error message you got. When I load it from the table though, it is fine and only gets corrupted when I call the next line

> camOPTMatrix <- read.csv(file = "camOPTMatrix.csv"), row.names = 1, check.names = FALSE, header =T)
> colnames(camOPTMatrix)

[13] "2018-08-15" "2018-08-16" "2018-08-17" "2018-08-18" "2018-08-19" "2018-08-20" "2018-08-21" "2018-08-22" "2018-08-23" "2018-08-24" "2018-08-25" "2018-08-26"
[25] "2018-08-27" "2018-08-28" "2018-08-29" "2018-08-30" "2018-08-31" "2018-09-01" "2018-09-02" "2018-09-03" "2018-09-04" "2018-09-05" "2018-09-06" "2018-09-07"
[37] "2018-09-08" "2018-09-09" "2018-09-10" "2018-09-11" "2018-09-12" "2018-09-13" "2018-09-14" "2018-09-15" "2018-09-16"
> names(camOPTMatrix)<- as.Date(names(camOPTMatrix),"%d/%m/%Y")
> colnames(camOPTMatrix)
 [1] NA NA NA NA NA NA NA NA NA NA NA NA NA NA NA NA NA NA NA NA NA NA NA NA NA NA NA NA NA NA NA NA NA NA NA NA NA NA NA NA NA NA NA NA NA

When I use the faulty camOPTMatrix (without column names) in spatialDetectionHistory, I get.the same error you had.

When I fix the column names, it is

Error: record date outside camera operation date range:  Station26

But that is a problem with your data, not the package. It got me thinking though and in the next version this situation will give a warning, not an error.
I will attach a preview of the next version here for you to try. Please let me know if the error persists (it does not for me, the function produces the desired output with three warnings):

Warning messages:
1: timeZone is not specified. Assuming UTC 
2: record date after camera operation date range:  Station26 
3: 1 records out of 168 were removed because they were taken after the end of the last occasion
Station26: 2018-09-19 01:18:46 


Please be careful though, this new version not properly tested yet and may contain unexpected bugs.

All the best,
Jürgen
